## HIGH-priority finding details

### H-1: Secrets panel is a stub; secrets management is split between Settings and Projects  (2/3 runs)

- **Docs**: `reference/admin-ui.mdx` — the `### Secrets` section described two functional sub-panels (Per-team secrets and Global secrets) as though they were accessible from a dedicated Secrets sidebar item, with API paths and `<Warning>` constraints. The `### Settings` section described only Fly sessions configuration with no mention of global secrets management.
- **Source**: `src/admin-ui/pages/stubs.ts:78-87` — the `secrets` sidebar route renders a "Coming soon" / "Partially implemented" placeholder that redirects operators to Projects (per-team) and Settings (global); `src/admin-ui/pages/settings.ts:33-57` — Settings is where global machine secrets are actually listed, created, and deleted.
- **Edit**: Replaced the Secrets section with a `<Note>` noting the placeholder state and bullet-pointed pointers to the correct panels. Expanded Settings to document its second function — global machine secrets management.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in 1/3 runs (Run 1); MEDIUM in 1/3 runs (Run 3). Kept HIGH per no-downgrade rule.

### H-2: JIRA_TOKEN/JIRA_CLOUD_ID/JIRA_SITE_URL listed as required target-repo secrets but no workflow reads them  (1/3 runs)

- **Docs**: `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` — the "Target-repo workflow secrets" tab Jira accordion declared `JIRA_TOKEN`, `JIRA_CLOUD_ID`, and `JIRA_SITE_URL` as required secrets for Jira-backed target repos, with a `<Warning>` that "all secrets for that provider must be configured for the target repo's workflows to function."
- **Source**: `workflows/claude-implement.yml:166-181`, `workflows/claude-plan.yml:321-355`, `workflows/comment-trigger.yml:204-213` — none of the three synced workflow files include any Jira credential in their `env` blocks. Jira status updates flow through the orchestrator's own runtime credentials via the runner callback, not through target-repo secrets.
- **Edit**: Replaced the Jira accordion content with a `<Tip>` explaining that Jira credentials are not configured in target-repo secrets. Removed the incorrect `<Warning>` implying both providers require target-repo secrets. Updated the Credentials at a glance table to show Jira credentials as "Orchestrator only."
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in 1/3 runs (Run 2).

### H-3: GAP_FILL_TRIGGER_SECRET description claims comment-trigger.yml POSTs to /trigger/gap-fill, but current synced workflow runs pipeline directly  (1/3 runs)

- **Docs**: `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` — described `GAP_FILL_TRIGGER_SECRET` as "the endpoint that synced `comment-trigger.yml` workflows POST to when a user comments `/ai-implement` on a PR."
- **Source**: `workflows/comment-trigger.yml:204-219` — the current synced `comment-trigger.yml` runs the pipeline directly via the runner container and never calls `/trigger/gap-fill`. The endpoint is still implemented (`src/gap-fill-trigger.ts:44`) but is not called by the standard workflow.
- **Edit**: Rewrote the `GAP_FILL_TRIGGER_SECRET` description to accurately state the endpoint dispatches implementation runs when called externally, and noted that the standard `comment-trigger.yml` runs the pipeline directly without calling this endpoint.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in 1/3 runs (Run 2).

### H-4: Planning pipeline steps not overridable via `custom/steps/`  (1/3 runs)

- **Docs**: `customize/custom-steps.mdx` — stated "Any of them can be overridden by placing a matching file in `custom/steps/`" for all 14 built-in step IDs, including planning steps (`architecture-analysis`, `explore-codebase`, `test-plan`, `work-unit-decomposition`, `cross-story-context`, `post-to-ticketing`) and the `implement`/`review` sub-steps.
- **Source**: `src/pipeline/planning-pipeline.ts:105-113` — the planning runner's `createPlanningRunner()` directly registers built-in step implementations with no call to `resolveModuleImport`, so `custom/steps/` is never consulted for planning steps; `src/pipeline/default-pipeline.ts:20-27` — the autonomous pipeline only checks `custom/steps/` for six IDs: `clone`, `install`, `feedback-loop`, `preflight`, `push`, `post-push-review`; `src/pipeline/steps/feedback-loop.ts:3-4` — `implement` and `review` are imported directly and are not individually resolvable.
- **Edit**: Replaced the "any of them can be overridden" claim with the accurate scope (six implementation pipeline steps support overrides). Added a `<Warning>` specifying that planning pipeline steps silently ignore any matching `custom/steps/` file, and that `implement`/`review` must be customized by overriding `feedback-loop`.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in 1/3 runs (Run 3).

## MEDIUM-priority finding details

### M-1: Admin UI sidebar Note omits 5 stub panels operators will see  (3/3 runs)

- **Docs**: `reference/admin-ui.mdx:9-16` — the opening `<Note>` lists Configure as three items (Projects, Pipelines & steps, Models & providers) and Developer as two items (Audit log, Customizations).
- **Source**: `src/admin-ui/sidebar.ts:14-34` — Configure has five items (adds Triggers & channels and Policies & risk); Developer has five items (adds MCP server, Webhooks, and Updates). All five additional items are rendered as stub pages via `src/admin-ui/pages/stubs.ts`.

### M-2: `setup/target-repo.mdx` presents `sync-workflow.yml` manual run as primary sync method  (2/3 runs)

- **Docs**: `setup/target-repo.mdx:13-35` — Step 2 directs users to run `gh workflow run sync-workflow.yml -f target_repo=your-org/your-repo` as the primary method for syncing workflow files into target repos.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/CLAUDE.md:150` — "`.github/workflows/sync-workflow.yml` remains as a manual fallback, but normal distribution should happen from the orchestrator" via the Projects panel's **Sync workflows** row action. The `reference/admin-ui.mdx` confirms: "This is the normal way to push workflow updates from the orchestrator into target repos."

### M-3: `teamKey` ParamField description is Linear-only despite also covering Jira  (2/3 runs)

- **Docs**: `configuration/team-repo-mappings.mdx:16-18` — `teamKey` ParamField says "Your Linear team identifier (e.g. `ENG`). This is the short prefix shown in Linear issue identifiers." The surrounding `<Tip>` does note Jira uses an arbitrary identifier, but the ParamField body itself describes only the Linear use case.
- **Source**: `src/config.ts:25` — `teamKey` is the primary key for all mappings regardless of provider; for Jira it is an operator-chosen label with no corresponding concept in Jira.

### M-4: `planningEnabled` description says planning posts to Linear — Jira mappings also supported  (1/3 runs)

- **Docs**: `configuration/team-repo-mappings.mdx:67-68` — the `planningEnabled` `<ParamField>` body reads "the orchestrator dispatches the planning workflow first, Claude posts structured analysis to Linear, and then implementation proceeds."
- **Source**: `src/pipeline/planning-pipeline.ts:25-101` — the planning pipeline's `post-to-ticketing` step routes through the mapping's configured ticketing provider, not Linear specifically; `src/providers/jira.ts` — JiraProvider implements the same TicketingProvider interface and receives planning comments when `ticketingProvider: jira` is set.

## LOW-priority findings (aggregate, numbered as L-1 … L-7)

- **L-1** — `reference/admin-ui.mdx:40` describes the Pipelines panel as "the dispatch log under its real internal name (`jobs` in the sidebar)" — `jobs` is only the route key, not the displayed sidebar label (Run 1; 1/3 runs)
- **L-2** — `reference/admin-ui.mdx:132` cites `src/pipeline/*.yml` as an internal source path in reader-facing prose; no `.yml` files exist under `src/pipeline/` — the actual built-in pipeline YAML is `pipelines/autonomous.yml` (Run 1, Run 3; 2/3 runs)
- **L-3** — `providers/anthropic.mdx:116` lists `claude-opus-4-7` as a valid example model ID; current generation is `claude-opus-4-8`. Model IDs are passed verbatim so the older ID would fail at invocation (Run 1, Run 3; 2/3 runs)
- **L-4** — `claude-implement.yml` defaults runner image to `:next` tag; `comment-trigger.yml` defaults to `:latest`; `environment-variables.mdx` documents `SESSION_IMAGE` defaulting to `:latest`. The `:next` vs `:latest` inconsistency across files may confuse operators comparing modes (Run 1, Run 2; 2/3 runs)
- **L-5** — `reference/labels.mdx:110` says the `/ai-implement` comment trigger requires "write access" but `comment-trigger.yml:61` accepts `write`, `maintain`, or `admin` roles — docs understate accepted permissions (Run 2; 1/3 runs)
- **L-6** — `await_ci` is declared as a `StepType` in `src/pipeline/types.ts:13` but has no corresponding step file and is not documented; appears to be a reserved future type (Run 3; 1/3 runs)
- **L-7** — `ai-implement/CLAUDE.md` lists built-in step keys as `clone`, `install`, `feedback-loop`, `preflight`, `push` but omits `post-push-review`, which is also registered as an overridable step in `src/pipeline/default-pipeline.ts:25` (Run 3; 1/3 runs — not a docs-repo file)
